cards.anchor: P1 registration enables P2 requests, but the account that every registered pending identity needs recognition fails: N1 is recognized while still pending. Bulk grouping of genuinely unmet receipts survives.
cards.burden: Registration clerk performs six validations; dispatcher performs six requests and compares boundary ledgers. Readable ledgers add no clerk labor. Record registrations, distinct recognitions, actions, failures and duplicates separately.
cards.construction: At boundary 0 compare pending identities with first-success recognition. Because N1 is pending and recognized, select individuals during its stale-display window. Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request N2,N3,N4 individually at ticks 0,1,2; idle dispatcher at 3. At boundary 4 require N1 and prior recognized notices cleared and queue empty, then bulk N5,N6. Request N7 individually at 5 and N8 at 6. If the guard fails, withhold bulk and declare this schedule unqualified.
cards.defeat: Reject if boundary-0 ledgers contradict stipulated N1 recognition, boundary-4 guard fails, any intended first delivery fails, dispatcher exceeds six actions, or boundary 9 lacks eight registrations and eight distinct recognitions.
cards.mutation: Turn the protected N1 pending/recognition mismatch into a sensor selecting WHEN bulk acts and WHERE early individual requests target. Pending without recognition instead diagnoses genuine unmet receipt demand and does not trigger the stale-display branch.
cards.prediction_candidate: Finite-model hypothesis: no N1 duplicate; first receipts N2,N3,N4 at ticks 1,2,3 and N5,N6,N7,N8 at 5,6,7,8. Eight registrations finish at boundary 6; eight recognitions including initial N1 finish by boundary 9 using six actions.
cards.prediction_rival: Immediate bulk includes recognized N1 and predicts duplicate service at tick 1. If recognition were absent, that pending identity would indicate unmet demand instead; this counterfactual is diagnostic, not an observed alternative case.
cards.probe: Read registration, recognition and pending ledgers at boundary 0, then queue and clearing states at boundary 4. Compare the modeled initial bulk trace with the conditional trace: pending plus prior first success separates stale display from missing recognition; tick-1 N1 duplicate separates immediate bulk from the guarded action.
cards.rival: Immediate routine bulk treating registered pending identities as unmet receipt demand.
unknowns: N1 delay origin remains unknown; fixed clearing proves no wider defect.
Later sender adaptation is unobserved and cannot change present fixed demand.
No empirical trial or globally best schedule proof is supplied; the trace predicts this finite model only.
